thread:
Anya: quick q — we're seeing SQS delayed-retry paths drop tracing baggage when the header > ~380 bytes, any prior art for compacting OTEL baggage?
Mike: yup seen that. SQS and some proxies chop non-printable or large headers.
Sara: short answer: either shrink baggage or put an opaque blob header and rehydrate at worker. tradeoffs though.
Anya: experiment: we packed attrs into a single header `X-RW-CTX` as base64(gzip(json(...))). reduced size but added decode CPU on ingress.
Mike: how heavy was decode? numbers?
Anya: in node POC ~0.5-0.9ms per request at p99 with our lambda runtime. acceptable for most gateways.
Sara: exporter compatibility is concern — most exporters (OTLP/Jaeger) expect distinct span attributes, not an opaque payload. we'd have to rehydrate before export.
Mike: rehydration could blow up downstream storage if we just inline everything. need sanitization/whitelist.
Anya: idea: hybrid mode — keep minimal keys in standard OTEL baggage (`txn.id`, `sampling.*`) and place verbose attrs in `X-RW-CTX` opaque blob. Gateway sets `x-rw-ctx-opaque: 1` when used.
Sara: sounds reasonable. consumers try to read `X-RW-CTX` if present; otherwise fall back to OTEL baggage.
Mike: what about SDKs that auto-propagate baggage? they'd duplicate keys if we don't strip.
Anya: gateway ingress should dedupe: if `X-RW-CTX` exists, drop overlapping baggage keys to avoid double-counting.
Sara: also need policy for exporters: rehydrate but drop large debug traces or `debug_payload` keys before sending to OTLP/infra. storage + retention hit otherwise.
Mike: propose config knobs: `trace.max_export_payload_bytes` and `trace.export_sanitize_keys` to control that behavior.
Anya: UX note — console should indicate `partial context` if we trimmed fields on export. helps SREs when investigating odd missing attributes.
Sara: what about signed/secure blobs? opaque header could be tampered with if passing across partners. we should HMAC the blob with service key.
Mike: yep. add `X-RW-CTX-SIG: sha256=base64(hmac(blob))`. gateway verifies.
Anya: draft header example we used in POC: ```
X-RW-CTX: eJyrVkrLz1eyUkpKLFKqBQAQeQbK
X-RW-CTX-SIG: sha256=abc...
x-rw-ctx-opaque: 1
```
Sara: also tried CBOR vs JSON inside blob. CBOR saved ~20% size, but makes debugging less human-friendly.
Mike: tradeoffs. CBOR + gzip gets best compactness, decode cost still within our budget.
Anya: perf results from staging POC: success rate for delayed retries improved from 91% -> 93% (fewer header drops). avg extra CPU per gateway 0.7ms.
Sara: exporter note: Jaeger agent in some envs chokes if we add too many attributes; so sanitize list mandatory.
Mike: propose RFC: - hybrid header approach - HMAC-signed opaque blob - gateway dedupe + rehydrate - exporter sanitize + config knobs - console badge for trimmed context
Anya: I'll write RFC draft. owners: @Mike @Anya. I'll include sample code for encode/decode and test harness.
Mike: I'll add perf numbers and config schema.
Sara: I'll include exporter sanitization rules and retention impact calc.
infra-bot: deploy queued | job=ctx-blob-poc | env=staging
deploy-bot: RFC PR opened -> https://git.example/repo/rfcs/678
Anya: thanks! tagging @platform-leads for visibility :eyes:
